identity.title: High-velocity extended molecular outflow in the star-formation dominated luminous infrared galaxy ESO 320-G030

paper_type_evidence.quote: we analyze new Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array (ALMA) CO(2–1) high spatial resolution ($\sim$60 pc) observations of the local ($d=48$ Mpc; scale of 240 pc arcsec$^{-1}$) LIRG ESO 320-G030

evidence.quote: local ($d=48$ Mpc; scale of 240 pc arcsec$^{-1}$) LIRG ESO 320-G030 ($\log L_{\rm IR}\slash \hbox{$L_{\rm \odot}$}= 11.3$; also known as IRAS F11506-3851)

question.value: Characterize the resolved massive molecular outflow in the star-formation dominated LIRG ESO 320-G030 and establish the nature of its obscured nucleus that drives it

evidence.quote: The main goals of this work are: characterize the resolved massive molecular outflow detected in this object and establish the nature of the extremely obscured nucleus which produces the massive molecular outflow.
as part of the project 2013.1.00271.S (PI: L. Colina)

claims.hypothesis: Is there a resolved massive molecular outflow in ESO 320-G030?
claims.experiment: Search for CO(2-1) emission deviating >200 km/s from a rotating-disk model
claims.result: Seven clumps, sizes 60–150 pc, masses 10^5.5–10^6.4 Msun, velocities ~370–540 km/s, total 10^6.8 Msun
claims.finding: A ~2.5 kpc clumpy molecular outflow originates in the nucleus

evidence.quote: We spatially resolve a high velocity ($\sim$450 km s$^{-1}$) outflow containing 10$^{6.8}$ $M_{\rm \odot}$ of molecular gas

claims.hypothesis: Is the nucleus powered by star formation rather than an AGN?
claims.experiment: Multiwavelength SED, radio spectral index, SFR and SN rates
claims.result: alpha=0.7, nuclear SFR ~15 Msun/yr, no AGN indicators
claims.finding: Highly obscured intense star formation powers the nucleus

evidence.quote: No evidence for the presence of an AGN is found.

claims.hypothesis: Can supernovae power the molecular outflow?
claims.experiment: Compare outflow kinetic energy and momentum with SN output

evidence.quote: The kinetic energy and radial momentum of the outflow represent $\sim$2% and 20%, respectively, of the SNe output.

claims.hypothesis: Does the outflow quench star formation or escape the galaxy?
claims.experiment: Loading factor and comparison with escape velocity
claims.result: Loading factor ~0.1–0.5; velocities below escape velocity 530 km/s
claims.finding: Quenching not efficient; gas likely returns to the disk

evidence.quote: The velocity of the outflowing clumps is lower than the escape velocity, so it is likely that most of this molecular gas will return to the disk after several Myr.

why_this_method.value: ULIRG-like CO conversion factor adopted since the factor for outflows is poorly known, giving lower limits

evidence.quote: The CO-to-H$_2$ conversion factor for outflows is poorly known.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Blue/red regions could be coplanar non-circular (radial) motions, rejected since velocity is too high for density-wave-driven flows

evidence.quote: the high velocity of this gas (comparable to the rotation curve half amplitude) is much higher than that expected for density-wave-driven gas flows

limitations_admitted.value: Factor ~5 systematic uncertainty in mass from alpha_CO; masses are lower limits

evidence.quote: The uncertainty in the mass determination is dominated by the factor of $\sim$5 systematic uncertainty in the CO-to-H$_2$ conversion factor.

limitations_admitted.value: Origin of outflowing molecular gas unclear from available data

evidence.quote: is not clear from the available data

referee_caveats_inferred: Outflow geometry (perpendicular to disk) is assumed, affecting deprojected velocities and energies
Clump identification relies on a simple disk model; bar non-circular motions could contaminate
Hot H2 mass depends strongly on assumed extinction
Mass loading rate relies on a single assumed dynamical time
